body:
Planning vetting completed against the installed-file investigation and two independent architecture/technical-art reviews. Saved revision 1 contains 44 required work tickets and three milestone acceptance nodes. Dark Mechanicus validate_plan returned valid with zero errors and zero warnings. This is plan validation, not evidence that the overhaul or its capability probes have run.

Confirmed user scope: all human characters including troops; equivalent DD2 controls and visual quality with an original Bannerlord-fitting asset catalog. The single-player versus multiplayer question has not yet been answered. It remains an explicit required decision in the capability contract; dependent production cannot proceed on a guessed answer.

Review corrections incorporated: full option-capacity testing waits for rendering and clothed-body proofs; aging waits for render-context adapters; native channel semantics and existing appearance corpora are preserved; numeric performance and naval baselines precede production. Every asset/equipment/control/maturity entry stays in a complete coverage manifest. Original presets, material isolation, all rendering surfaces, nondestructive persistence and troop-seed semantics have explicit work and evidence. Pre-contract outfit inventory is provisional; final mixed soft/rigid acceptance has one owner. Early maturity attachment tests use diagnostic fixtures to avoid circular dependencies.

Three milestones allow discovery to expand the FUTURE production sprint into exact-ID bounded art, native-extension, shader/compositing, tool-repair and any required multiplayer batches before production starts. The graph was reduced from 248 initial dependency links to 77 equivalent links, then corrected with three genuine prerequisites. Every required ticket is covered by its own milestone acceptance node. Shared editor/game/import state has a single owner with acknowledged handoffs.

Remaining engine capability, art throughput, final catalog size and performance questions are executable prerequisites, not claimed facts. Production scope changes require an explicit decision; blocked requirements cannot be silently dropped. The epic is saved in Backlog; no execution run, game modification or implementation was started by this planning task. Source investigation: task-notes/character-overhaul.md. Related world, combat and creature epics were read for interface boundaries and were not edited by this task.
